sections.heading: The setup
sections.body: As of the Nov 23 close, the S&P 500 sits at 7,237, about 5.7% below its level a month ago and in the lower half of its 1-month range (high 7,744, low 6,910). The Nasdaq 100 is weaker still at 26,746, down 8.6% over the month and also in the lower half of its range. The VIX closed at 26.6, up from 19.5 a month ago, and the Euro Stoxx 50 is down 4.3% over the last five sessions. The week carries 32 scheduled reports from the S&P 500 / Russell 1000 / core universe, 16 of them in technology, with the busiest day on Thursday (13).

sections.heading: What to watch
sections.body: Monday: ORCL (technology) and NKE (consumer-cyclical) report, along with CTAS and PAYX in industrials. Tuesday: MDB and OKTA lead the software names. Wednesday: SNOW and ZS report in technology, and FIVE in consumer-cyclical. Thursday is the heaviest day, with DG and HRL in consumer-defensive, ULTA in consumer-cyclical, and DOCU, PATH and RBRK in technology. All 32 dates are still estimated, so confirm each against company announcements.

sections.heading: Signals to trust
sections.body: Mining (+4.63% median 3-day reaction, 229 tickers, 2,766 news items) leads the reaction table, followed by copper (-2.53%, 6 tickers, 231 news items) and energy (+1.98%, 328 tickers, 5,164 news items, a thick window). None of this week's 32 reporters sit in those three sectors. The sectors reporting this week are flat by comparison: technology -0.02% median across 810 tickers (11,842 news items), consumer-cyclical +0.32% and consumer-defensive -0.47%.
